candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — end-of-life care, symptom relief, and comfort measures
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — end-of-life comfort care
candidate.educational_objective: Prioritize multidimensional comfort and the client's goals during end-of-life care.

options.A: Limit direct care and interaction to avoid all stimulation.
options.B: Set aside the client's expressed wishes whenever the care team prefers a different plan.
options.C: Continue burdensome curative treatment regardless of the client's goals.
options.D: Relieve pain and other distressing symptoms while supporting emotional, spiritual, practical, and family needs according to the client's wishes.

candidate.rationale: The NIH National Institute on Aging describes end-of-life care as addressing physical comfort, mental and emotional needs, spiritual needs, and practical concerns, while supporting family and following the person's end-of-life wishes. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: End-of-life care should follow the person's wishes and address physical comfort, emotional/mental needs, spiritual needs, practical concerns, and support for family.
candidate.source_document_title: Providing Care and Comfort at the End of Life
